# Vector Store - Spring AI and Ollama API

This example demonstrates how to store text in an in-memory vector store and
query it with various terms using a locally hosted embedding model via
[Ollama](https://ollama.com/). Ollama is an open-source platform and
command-line tool that enables developers to download, manage, and run LLMs
entirely on local machines—eliminating reliance on cloud APIs, access keys, or
privacy-related concerns. It supports multimodal inputs, tool invocation, and
integrations with REST and 
[Java](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/embeddings/ollama-embeddings.html), 
making it well suited for prototyping, debugging, and deploying LLM-powered
applications in a fully offline, customisable environment.

This example also uses [Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai), a
Java-based framework for building LLM-driven applications. It provides tools for
prompt management, LLM call chaining, memory handling, retrieval-augmented
generation (RAG), and integration with external data sources—all within the
Java ecosystem.

An alternative is [LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j),
which similarly provides an abstraction layer between LLMs and applications.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download)

## Run the example

1. Download and setup Ollama

   If you haven’t already, please download and install Ollama from the
   [official download page](https://ollama.com/download), following the
   instructions provided. Ollama includes a command-line tool for managing and
   interacting with it.

   Models must be downloaded from a repository, such as the
   [Ollama Library](https://ollama.com/library) or
   [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/models). Ensure the model is saved in
   a supported format, such as
   [GPT-Generated Unified Format (GGUF)](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/gguf).

   To list models installed locally, run:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   After a fresh installation, no models will be listed.

   ```
   NAME                       ID              SIZE      MODIFIED
   ```

   To get started, download
   [mxbai-embed-large](https://ollama.com/library/mxbai-embed-large) with:

   ```shell
   ollama pull mxbai-embed-large
   ```

   This process may take a few seconds to several minutes, depending on your
   internet connection.

   ```
   pulling manifest
   pulling 819c2adf5ce6: 100% ▕██████████████████▏ 669 MB
   pulling c71d239df917: 100% ▕██████████████████▏  11 KB
   pulling b837481ff855: 100% ▕██████████████████▏   16 B
   pulling 38badd946f91: 100% ▕██████████████████▏  408 B
   verifying sha256 digest
   writing manifest
   success
   ```

   Once the model is downloaded, you can begin using it.

   (Optional) To confirm the model has been installed, list the models again:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   You should now see `mxbai-embed-large` in the list.

   ```
   NAME                        ID              SIZE      MODIFIED
   mxbai-embed-large:latest    468836162de7    669 MB    Less than a second ago
   ```

   To verify that Ollama is running and accessible on the default port `11434`,
   use:

   ```shell
   curl --silent --show-error 'http://localhost:11434/api/tags' | jq
   ```

   This will return a list of available models.

   ```
   {
     "models": [
       {
         "name": "mxbai-embed-large:latest",
         "model": "mxbai-embed-large:latest",
         "modified_at": "2077-05-27T12:34:56.789000000Z",
         "size": 669615493,
         "digest": "468836162de7f81e041c43663fedbbba921dcea9b9fefea135685a39b2d83dd8",
         "details": {
           "parent_model": "",
           "format": "gguf",
           "family": "bert",
           "families": [
             "bert"
           ],
           "parameter_size": "334M",
           "quantization_level": "F16"
         }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

   To interact with the embedding model, run:

   ```shell
   curl --silent --show-error 'http://localhost:11434/api/embeddings' \
     --data '{
       "model": "mxbai-embed-large",
       "prompt": "Humans first landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission."
   }'
   ```

   This will return the embeddings for the given text

   When using Ollama via the REST API, as in the following steps, the required
   model must be downloaded in advance. Ollama does not automatically download
   missing models when accessed through the REST API. Please ensure the
   `mxbai-embed-large` model is available before proceeding.

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `mxbai-embed-large` model is available. For further details, please refer to
   Step 1.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (_Optional_) Verify that the application was created.

   ```shell
   tree --prune --sort=name -L 1 './target'
   ```

   The application Fat JAR file

   ```
   ./target
   ├── vector-store-springai-ollama-api-1.0.0.jar
   └── vector-store-springai-ollama-api-1.0.0.jar.original

   0 directories, 2 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `mxbai-embed-large` model is available. For further details, please refer to
   Step 1.

   ```shell
   java \
     -jar './target/vector-store-springai-ollama-api-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   The program will populate the vector datastore with some text and then
   performs some queries.
